newsitem.title: UK: Eurotherm says remains positive on future.
newsitem.headline: Eurotherm says remains positive on future.

text.p: British industrial electronic equipment manufacturer Eurotherm Plc said on Tuesday the company remained positive about the group's medium and long-term prospects even if the sterling continued to strengthen.
The company announced a 21.4 percent dip in pre-tax profits for the six-month period to April 30, 1997 on a turnover of 99.5 million stg, down from 102.2 million the previous year.
Eurotherm's operations were hit by the appreciation of the British pound without which the company's underlying sales rose 5.7 percent at constant currency.
The company's return on sales slipped to 14.8 percent against 18.3 percent in the previous year.
Chairman James Hann said Eurotherm was now looking at strengthening its markets in North America and in the Far East.
"...Your board is actively investigating ways of achieving better penetration in these substantial markets," he said.
The company said it gained market shares in new temperature controllers and graphic recorders during the first half.
